targets.text: The chat console's public sign-in can't be used to burn the mail quota, mail strangers or raise false alarms, and it warns when its bot check is off
Every behaviour in c10 is shown by automated tests against a real guest store, with only the mail adapter faked.

A persistent global budget caps guest code mail per hour and per day, counted before the send is scheduled because sends run in background tasks (web/entry.py:552,569), covering the guest-code paths at entry.py:668 and :989. It reuses the attempts table helpers (guest_store.py:565-592); retention there is one day (ATTEMPT_RETENTION_S), so a daily window needs margin added.
The budget survives a restart, is counted before the send is scheduled, and its daily window can't lapse early from attempts-table retention.
Approved users' sign-in code, new-browser notice and set-password mail stay outside the budget (entry.py:663,732; setpw.py:196-205), so guests can never lock an owner out of signing in.
No approved-mail path checks or increments the guest budget, and a test proves it with the budget exhausted.

Reserved domains are refused before any provider call, keeping the same status, page, pending cookie, pad floor, attempt counting and dummy verify as a normal submission (entry.py:653-678), so a refusal reveals nothing.
Status, page, cookie and pad floor match a normal guest submission, and the attempt is still counted, shown by a test comparing the two responses.

Provider failures are classified so recipient errors don't alert, each failure logs its HTTP status but never the address or body, and failed sends are counted in metrics. classify (alerts.py:48) separates only 429 today; MailSendError.status exists; failures log the type alone (entry.py:549,571).
No log line or alert contains an address, code or provider body, and a real outage's alert isn't suppressed by an earlier recipient error.

With guest mode on and no bot check configured, the console warns at startup and in doctor, and a setting can refuse guest codes in that state. make_bot_verifier silently returns NoopVerifier (entry.py:193-200), and doctor (cli/_meta.py:317) has no such check.
With guest mode on and keys absent, startup logs one warning and doctor reports it; with keys set, neither does; and approved sign-in works in every mode.
No change to the approved sign-in flow or its alerts; irc-lens#69 owns those.
The approved sign-in code path has no behaviour change apart from budget exemption, shown by the existing sign-in tests passing unchanged.
The operators of a public irc-lens console, who get the delivery alerts and pay for the mail quota, and the guests and approved users who rely on sign-in mail arriving.
Operators can read the new warning, status logs and counters without reading guests.db.
Scripted traffic can't spend more guest mail than the budget, a bad address raises no alert, every failed send logs its HTTP status, and a console with no bot check says so at startup and in doctor.
Each clause maps to at least one test that fails on main today.

On 2026-11-04 a scripted client submitted the sign-in form with a reserved address. The console called the mail provider, the send failed, and operators got an alert saying codes weren't being delivered, while delivery was fine. Nothing logged the status.
The scenario replays from the same input in a test: a reserved address no longer reaches the adapter or raises an alert.

Guest mail is the one thing an anonymous visitor can make the console spend: enough rotating addresses can use up the quota, and that also stops approved users' sign-in codes. False alarms teach operators to ignore the alert that matters.
Approved mail really is exempt: with the budget used up, the approved sign-in path still calls the adapter.

In a test driving 200 guest submissions with rotating addresses from one IP, no more than the configured hourly budget reach the mail adapter, 0 reserved-domain addresses reach it, 0 recipient errors raise an alert, and an approved user's sign-in code still sends with the budget at 0.
The test uses the real limit and budget code with a fake clock, not a mocked limiter.

Clef is a layer in the console's threat detection, across public traffic and not only sign-in: fixed rules watch counts of sign-in activity, mail spend, probed paths, 401 and 403 responses, and when a window crosses a trigger the console sends the decider (Clef, general domain) counts only and raises an operator alert with its threat verdict and the numbers. Clef detects and never enforces; the bot check, limits and budget do the blocking.
Sign-in never waits on or fails because of the decider: with the decider down, sign-in is unchanged and the numbers still reach the operator, marked as not assessed.

The decider receives derived counts only, never addresses, IPs, user agents, paths or any other visitor-supplied string, so a visitor can't write into its prompt or send personal data across the mesh.
Verdicts are checked against labelled windows, including a real group of guests behind one IP, before the alert is trusted, and its misses are recorded.
A budget hit or a burst always alerts, whatever the decider says, so a wrong 'genuine' can't hide abuse.

Threat detection stays cheap and can't be driven by attackers. Counting per request is in memory, with no database write or network call. Clef runs at most once per 15-minute window and at most 24 times a day, only after a rule triggers, with one call in flight, a 5 second timeout and no retries or queue: a skipped call is dropped and the alert says not assessed. These caps are config defaults and hold under any traffic volume.
A test driving 10000 requests in a window with a fake clock and fake decider sees at most 1 Clef call, a fixed-size counter state, and no added database writes on the request path.
With the decider hanging, request latency is unchanged and the event loop isn't blocked, because the call runs off the request path with the timeout enforced.

All outgoing mail has a total ceiling below the provider quota, and set-password and delete-confirm mail get an hourly per-address limit. Today web/setpw.py post_password and web/deletion.py post_request allow 10 mails per minute per address with no bot check, to anyone who knows an approved or guest address.
With guest budget unused, a test driving set-password or delete requests for one known address can't exceed its hourly limit, and total sends can't exceed the ceiling.

The guest budget gets an hourly per-IP cap beside it, and exhausting the budget is treated as a denial of guest sign-in, not only as protection: 20 scripted posts an hour would stop real guests, who still see the normal code page because entry.py keeps responses identical.
A test shows one IP can't use the whole hourly budget, and the budget-hit alert says real guests may be getting no mail.
Operators can lift or reset the budget and turn off required bot check through config, with no code change, and the rollback steps are documented.
A rehearsal in a test environment restores guest mail with a config change and a restart.

Clef detection is optional and off by default: decider URL and credential come from config and an env var, and a deployment with no gateway, such as a standby host or an outside user of irc-lens, runs every other layer unchanged.
With no decider configured, startup is clean, rules still alert, and alerts say not assessed.

Probe counting uses route matching in middleware, not status codes: anonymous requests to real and nonexistent paths both get 401, because auth runs first (auth.py:97 reads match_info), so status can't separate a probe from a mistake.
A test shows a nonexistent path counts as a probe and a real route's 401 doesn't.

tasks.summary: Make delivery alerts mean an outage
acceptance_criteria: A 422 or similar recipient error raises no alert and doesn't take the hourly slot; 401, 403, 429, 5xx and network failures alert under classified kinds
A failed send logs its HTTP status and never the address, code or provider body
Failed sends are counted in /owner/metrics
tasks.instruction: Own src/irc_lens/alerts.py, mail.py and tests/test_alerts.py. A 403 can be a sender problem or Cloudflare's agent block, so keep it alerting as its own kind and say both in the text. Update the alert wording: it can fire for notice, set-password and delete mail too. The receiving Worker doesn't allow-list kinds.

tasks.summary: Refuse reserved addresses in the guest paths
acceptance_criteria: example.com, example.org, example.net, .invalid, .test and .localhost never reach the mail adapter
Status, body apart from the echoed address, cookie presence and timing floor match a normal guest submission
Replaying the Nov 4 submission calls no adapter and raises no alert
tasks.instruction: Check at web/entry.py:658 and :989, not inside _plausible_email, which admin.py and others share. Keep the dummy verify, attempt counting, pending cookie and pad floor.

acceptance_criteria: Past the hourly or daily budget no guest code reaches the adapter, and the count survives a restart
One IP alone can't use the whole hourly budget, while other IPs still get codes
With the guest budget at 0, an approved sign-in code still sends
Setting the budget in config to lift it restores guest mail after a restart, and the steps are documented
tasks.instruction: New src/irc_lens/mail_budget.py using guest_store attempts helpers, with config keys in config.py and docs/guest-mode-config.md. Count before the send task is scheduled, since sends run in the background. Attempts retention is exactly one day, so give the daily window margin. Keep sqlite calls off the event loop (see #72). Defaults 50 a day and 20 an hour; live values stay in private config.

tasks.summary: Limit set-password and delete mail, and cap total sends
acceptance_criteria: Repeat set-password or delete requests for one address stop reaching the adapter at the hourly per-address limit, with the page unchanged
Total sends never exceed the ceiling, whichever path sent them
tasks.instruction: Own web/setpw.py and web/deletion.py, and add the total ceiling at the shared send seam in mail.py send_with_alert, so every path is counted. Approved sign-in codes pass only the total ceiling, which sits below the provider quota.

tasks.summary: Warn on a missing bot check, and keep trusted browsers working
acceptance_criteria: Guest mode on with no keys gives one startup warning and a doctor finding; with keys set, neither
With verify failing, a trusted approved browser signs in and an untrusted one doesn't
With require_bot_check on and no keys, guest codes are refused and approved sign-in works
Existing approved sign-in tests pass unchanged
tasks.instruction: Own make_bot_verifier in web/entry.py, serve startup, and a doctor check. require_bot_check defaults off in this task's first release; turning it on is a rollout step. Trusted browsers skip verify only for approved sign-in, per decision c26. Read _post_signin_app closely: correct = human and pw_ok today.

tasks.summary: Count threat signals cheaply on the request path
acceptance_criteria: An unrouted path counts as a probe, and a 401 on a real route doesn't
10000 requests in a window leave counter state at a fixed size, with no database write or network call on the request path
tasks.instruction: New src/irc_lens/threat.py and one middleware. Use match_info to tell an unrouted path from a refused real route: anonymous requests get 401 either way. Counters only, fixed size, with distinct-source counts capped and hashed in memory, reset each 15-minute window. Reading user agents to classify is fine; no raw strings are kept.

acceptance_criteria: A window crossing any trigger raises one alert with its counts, within the existing hourly limit per kind
A budget-hit alert says real guests may be getting no mail
A lone guest's normal window raises nothing
tasks.instruction: New rules module beside threat.py. Starting triggers: refused responses at 50 or more, entry posts at 10 or more, any reserved address, any failed send, any budget hit. All are config values. Urgency comes from the rules, not Clef. Check thresholds against counters again before trusting them.

tasks.summary: Add Clef as an optional, bounded verdict
acceptance_criteria: The request body holds derived counts only, enforced by a test on the built request
With the decider down or hanging, sign-in latency is unchanged and the alert goes out marked not assessed
With no decider configured, startup is clean and all other layers work
The call caps hold in a test with a fake clock and fake decider
tasks.instruction: New src/irc_lens/decider.py, off by default, with URL in config and credential from an env var. Runs off the request path. At most 1 call per window and 24 a day, one in flight, 5 second timeout, no retries or queue. Build the request from counters so that no visitor string can reach it. The verdict is labelled advisory.

tasks.summary: Test Clef on labelled windows before trusting its verdict
acceptance_criteria: Results list each window, the label, the verdict and the misses, with the count of real versus made-up windows
No mail-abuse window is missed before the advisory label can be lifted
Load per call on the decider host is measured and recorded
tasks.instruction: A script over a labelled set of counts: real windows from counters once collected, plus made-up ones, including a real group behind one IP and a background scanner. Keep the windows held out from any prompt tuning. Measure the decider host's load per call and lower the 24-a-day default if needed. Record misses. The advisory label stays until the owner lifts it.

tasks.summary: Prove the whole stack end to end, and document it
acceptance_criteria: 200 rotating-address submissions from one IP: no more than the hourly budget reach the adapter, no reserved addresses reach it, no recipient errors alert, and an approved code still sends at budget 0
Each behaviour in the after-state has a test that fails on the pre-hardening code
An operator can see the warning, status logs and counters without opening guests.db
tasks.instruction: A real guest store with only the mail adapter and decider faked. Write docs/security-checklist.md and guest-mode-config.md for operators. Add the operator view in /owner/metrics.

tasks.summary: Roll out on the live console, with a rehearsed rollback
acceptance_criteria: Sign-in passes in a real browser on every path, through the Worker, with Turnstile on
Rollback restores guest mail by config in a timed rehearsal
Live values and bot check state aren't written to the public repo
tasks.instruction: With the owner, after the chat edge work is live. Set Turnstile keys in grant and enable them. Pass a real browser test directly and through the Worker, checking siteverify's visitor IP. Only then turn on require_bot_check. Set budget values in private config. Rehearse lifting the budget and turning the bot check off.

risks.text: Fallback task t6 changes client_ip in web/entry.py and auth.py, and this plan builds on it. Start after it merges to avoid a conflict.
Turnstile may not work through the Worker, because the visitor IP across the Worker-to-tunnel hop is unverified.
HTTP 403 is ambiguous, so its alert text has to cover both causes.
Bounces from rotating addresses may hurt the sending reputation even under budget; the provider's policy wasn't read.
web/entry.py is shared by the reserved-address, budget and bot check tasks, which are ordered to avoid conflicts.
